title: ts SDK: interoperability playbook for AsyncIterator <-> Web Streams consumption patterns
creator: Miguel Ortiz
description:
Background:
The TypeScript SDK currently supports two commonly requested streaming primitives: async iterators (for Node/TS consumers with for-await-of ergonomics) and browser-compatible Web Streams (ReadableStream). Different consumers (server-side middleware, edge runtimes, browser fetch handlers) expect one or the other, and we see many copies of small adapter utilities across apps and examples.

Problem statement:
- Inconsistent semantics across adapters: backpressure, cancellation, and error propagation differ between community snippets.
- Retry and resume semantics for partially-read streams are underspecified: when a streaming request fails mid-stream, higher-level retry logic does not have a safe resumption point in many consumer patterns.
- Dual consumption (accidentally reading the same logical stream twice) is a common footgun.
- Example gallery is fragmented; users copy/paste incompatible snippets (Node-only vs browser-only).

Goals:
1) Provide a small, well-tested adapter surface in the TS SDK with predictable semantics for conversion between AsyncIterator and Web Streams.
2) Ensure adapters preserve backpressure and cancellation (via AbortSignal) and surface errors identically.
3) Ship a short playbook + canonical examples covering: for-await-of, piping to Response, Node stream interop, and resume/retry patterns.
4) Add integration tests that run in Node and a browser-like environment (playwright) to validate interop behaviors.

Non-goals:
- Replace userland frameworks' stream primitives (we only provide helpers/adapters and docs).
- Implement full resumable streaming protocols (this ticket lays groundwork and docs for future resume tokens).

Proposed API surface (sketches):
- SDK streaming responses should expose a normalized stream object: { asAsyncIterator: () => AsyncIterable<Uint8Array>, asWebStream: (opts?: { preventCancel?: boolean }) => ReadableStream<Uint8Array>, toNodeReadable?: () => stream.Readable }
- Standalone helpers exported from @redwood/inference/streams:
  - asyncIteratorToWebStream(iterable: AsyncIterable<Uint8Array>, signal?: AbortSignal): ReadableStream<Uint8Array>
  - webStreamToAsyncIterator(stream: ReadableStream<Uint8Array>, signal?: AbortSignal): AsyncIterable<Uint8Array>
  - ensureSingleConsumer(streamLike): { getIterator(), getWebStream() } // guards against dual-consumption with helpful error message

Key behavioral contracts (must be preserved in tests):
- Cancellation: if the consumer AbortSignal is triggered, adapters must call underlying cancel/return where available and propagate an AbortError to the consumer.
- Error propagation: any error thrown by the underlying source must be rethrown from both async iterator and Web Stream consumers with consistent message and stack where possible.
- Backpressure: writing into a Web Stream created from an async iterator should not eagerly buffer unbounded data; use WritableStreamDefaultController.desiredSize to respect backpressure from the destination.
- Single-consumer guard: adapters should throw a clear error when multiple consumers attempt to read the same logical stream.

Retry semantics (guidance):
- For now: do not attempt transparent resume inside adapters. Instead provide a pattern in the playbook: checkpointing/resume token injected in each event, client-side checkpointing, and retry harness that restarts and fast-forwards the new stream until checkpoint.
- Long-term: coordinate with runtime teams to add a minimal resume token envelope on streaming protocol.

Examples to include in docs directory and SDK examples package:
- Browser: pipe SDK web stream into Response for streaming fetch endpoint response (Edge, Cloudflare Workers). Includes AbortController example.
- Node: for-await-of consume and pipe to http.ServerResponse using node stream utilities.
- Cross-runner: convert SDK AsyncIterator -> WebStream -> TextDecoderStream -> TransformStream (demo of composition).
- Retry playbook: pseudo-code showing token-based resume logic and safe retry boundaries.

Test plan:
- Unit tests for adapter functions that validate: cancellation, error propagation, backpressure semantics (using fake controllers), single-consumer guard.
- Integration test in Node.js: spawn a test server and consume via for-await-of and Node.Readable, verify cancellation flows.
- Integration test in browser-like environment: Playwright test that mounts a service worker or an endpoint and consumes Response.body via ReadableStream, asserting byte-level equality and early-cancel propagation.
- Performance regression smoke: adapter overhead must not exceed 5% median latency in our microbench harness (run against runtime-1.18).

Implementation milestones:
1) Design doc and API sketches (this ticket) — done.
2) Implement adapters and internal utilities with full types and JSDoc — owner: @lena-park.
3) Add unit tests and integration tests (playwright) — owner: @simon-choi.
4) Add examples to examples/ts-sdk and docs/playbook.
5) Release as part of sdk-ts-2.4.0 and publish migration notes.

Acceptance criteria:
- SDK exports the adapter helpers with full TS types and runtime tests.
- Playbook added to docs with at least 4 canonical examples and migration guidance.
- Integration tests pass in CI (Node + Playwright).
- No known regressions in existing streaming behavior (validated by running SDK regression suite).

Artifacts / links:
- Draft design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/TS+Streaming+Interop+Playbook
- Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/1832 (WIP)
- Example branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/examples/tree/ts-stream-playbook
- Internal microbench: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/sdks/streaming-adapters

Notes / trade-offs discussed:
- We intentionally avoid adding heavy runtime abstractions (no new protocol shaping) to keep the SDK surface small. That reduces implementation complexity but defers transparent resumability to later work.
- Exposing both primitives (async iterator + Web Stream) on the same returned object simplifies migration but requires careful single-consumer guarding to avoid confusing errors.

Open questions:
- Should the SDK make AbortSignal mandatory for adapters to ensure consistent cancellation semantics? (Design leaning: optional but recommended.)
- Do we want a small opt-in telemetry metric when a consumer cancels early to help tune backpressure? (Privacy/signal implications)

Next steps:
- Complete initial implementation PR (WIP link above), unblock CI tests, and solicit design review from platform infra (Tobias Meyer) and DX (Priya Shah).
- After review, land feature flag-gated release and update docs.
